section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to leave the interstate for an exit, you should:
options: a:Be in the proper lane at least one mile before your exit and do not slow until on the deceleration lane.,b:Signal and slow down 50–100 feet before the ramp.,c:Reduce to 45 mph one mile before exiting.,d:Stop in the exit lane before slowing.
note: Plan ahead by getting into the correct lane well before your exit and avoid slowing until you reach the deceleration lane."

question: When are roads especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement is often most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain as surface oils combine with water, creating a slick film.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on a county road without a hard surface is:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:55 miles per hour,c:50 miles per hour.,d:40 miles per hour.
note: The typical speed limit on unpaved county roads is 50 mph unless another limit is posted."

question: May you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal to drive at night using only parking lights; you must use headlights in conditions of reduced visibility.

question: As daylight begins to fade, what should you use to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Turn on low beam headlights as dusk approaches to help other drivers see you; reserve high beams for dark, open roads with no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: At a four-way stop, the driver on the right should insist on the right-of-way.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never insist on right-of-way in a way that could cause a crash; yield your legal right-of-way when doing so prevents an accident.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Slightly to the right.,b:Sharply away from the curb.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic and into the curb.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want the vehicle to travel; as it straightens, correct as needed.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Flash your headlights and proceed.,b:Speed up to pass before they cross.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Always slow and, if necessary, stop for pedestrians crossing the roadway. Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks and be especially cautious around children.

question: To pass a bicyclist safely, what should you do?
options: a:Drive into the bicycle lane until it is clear to pass.,b:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible when passing.,c:Honk to warn the bicyclist and then pass quickly.
note: When passing a bicycle, reduce speed and give the bicyclist plenty of room; do not crowd or force the rider off their line.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median, must you stop?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway separated by a median, you are not required to stop in most cases.

question: If the driver ahead appears distracted (driving with one hand and talking), how should you react?
options: a:Match their behavior to keep pace.,b:Give that vehicle extra space.,c:Honk continuously until they pay attention.
note: If another driver seems inattentive, increase the distance between vehicles. Distracted drivers have reduced reaction times and present a higher crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, when should you use the left lane?
options: a:To stop briefly,b:To overtake or pass another vehicle.,c:To prepare to exit.,d:To drive slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Use the left lane primarily for passing; remain in the right lanes for normal travel unless overtaking."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What happens to fines for speeding in work zones?
options: a:Doubled.,b:Reduced.,c:Tripled.
note: Fines for moving violations such as speeding are doubled in work zones where workers are present and in school zones during posted hours.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make eye contact then proceed at normal speed.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Slow down and pass carefully in front of them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and another vehicle arrive at a four-way stop at the same time and that vehicle is on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever signals first has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, yield to the vehicle on your right. If the other vehicle is on your left, you are to its right and have the right-of-way.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs instruct drivers on laws and regulations that must be obeyed; failure to do so may result in penalties.

question: If your accelerator suddenly sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Reach down to pull up the pedal.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn off the ignition while moving.
note: Keep your focus on driving, shift the car to neutral, apply steady braking, pull safely off the road, and turn off the engine once stopped.

question: By operating a motor vehicle in Nebraska, you have given implied consent to what?
options: a:Submit to a chemical test when requested by a law enforcement officer.,b:Refuse testing without consequence.,c:Choose which chemical test to take.
note: Nebraska’s Implied Consent law means drivers must submit to required chemical testing upon a lawful request by an officer; refusal may carry penalties.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.,b:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,c:Turn on your low-beam headlights.
note: Use low-beam headlights (not high beams) and reduce speed in fog because high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility further. Be prepared to stop if visibility is poor.

question: Under Nebraska law, children up to what age must be secured in a federally-approved child safety seat?
options: a:Four years old,b:Eight years old,c:Ten years old,d:Six years old
note: Children up to age six must be properly secured in a federally-approved child safety seat while in a moving vehicle."

question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,b:In order to see potential hazards early.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways you should scan farther ahead to detect potential hazards early, anticipate traffic changes, and react safely to merging traffic and sudden slowdowns.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Pull into the center lane and stop.,b:Slow down but stay in your lane and let it pass.,c:Drive faster to clear the road ahead.,d:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens: safely move to the right edge and stop until they have passed; if in an intersection drive through then stop."

question: After a train has passed and you have stopped at the crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed immediately when you see the train pass.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Both look for a second train and wait for warning signals to stop flashing before proceeding.
note: Even after one train passes, check for a second train on adjacent tracks and wait until all gates are up and warning lights have stopped before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As a green light turns yellow when you near an intersection, your best response is to:
options: a:Prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Apply the brakes sharply to stop immediately.,d:Turn right regardless of traffic
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon turn red; be prepared to stop safely rather than accelerating to beat it."

question: What can happen to bicyclists who do not obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are always given warnings instead of tickets.,b:They can be ticketed just like motor vehicle drivers.,c:They must ride on sidewalks only.,d:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles and may be cited for violations."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right.,c:Always watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Before you pass on a multilane highway, make sure the lane you intend to use is clear, signal, and complete the maneuver safely.

question: Are children under age 18 allowed to ride in a vehicle's cargo area?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nebraska law prohibits passengers under 18 from riding in cargo areas; children must be properly restrained in a seat belt or child safety seat while the vehicle is moving.

question: How should your following distance change when following a motorcycle?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Keep it the same as any vehicle.,c:Ignore motorcycle behavior.,d:Increase your following distance compared to following other vehicles.
note: Allow greater following distance because motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver check blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the left outside mirror.,b:Use only the rearview mirror.,c:Look over the left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly beside and slightly behind the vehicle; a quick glance over the appropriate shoulder verifies those blind spots before changing lanes.

question: If someone is tailgating you and there is no right lane, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and ignore them.,b:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to warn them off.,d:Speed up to increase the gap from the tailgater.
note: If tailgated and you cannot move right, slow down gradually when safe to encourage the tailgater to pass; never brake abruptly.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is used to:
options: a:Mark public recreation areas.,b:Indicate a stop requirement.,c:Provide mileage information.,d:Warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Using a handheld device to read, type, or send written messages while driving in Nebraska is:
options: a:Completely legal if you are stopped at a red light.,b:A secondary offense with a fine of $200–$500.,c:A secondary offense with a $50–$100 fine.,d:A primary offense.
note: It is a secondary offense to use a handheld device to read, type, or send written communication while driving; penalties range from $200 to $500.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,b:All of the above.,c:Tranquilizers
note: Prescription depressants, illegal drugs, and many over-the-counter medications (including some cough and cold remedies) can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, a driver should:
options: a:Take the right-of-way.,b:Proceed normally.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow and be prepared to yield to blind pedestrians who may be using canes or guide dogs; prioritize their safety.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should put on cruise control near the crossing.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always exercise caution near railroad tracks.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop unless traffic or other conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, how should you look?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Look directly through the rear window.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal and back quickly.
note: When reversing, look over your shoulder and through the rear window for the best view; do not rely solely on mirrors. Back up slowly.

question: What are truck “no zones”?
options: a:Zones where cars have plenty of following distance.,b:Areas several car lengths behind the truck.,c:Areas around large trucks where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck's ability to maneuver.,d:Designated safe zones for cars to pass trucks.
note: No zones are blind spots around large vehicles where cars may disappear from the truck driver’s view or be so close that they restrict the truck’s stopping and maneuvering ability."

question: Double solid yellow center lines on a roadway indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Prohibited from either direction.,c:Allowed only if traffic is light.,d:Allowed only if you signal.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic travels in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either side."

question: What minimum following distance should drivers maintain under normal conditions?
options: a:Five seconds.,b:Seven seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Allow at least three seconds of following distance under normal conditions and increase that distance when visibility or road conditions are poor.

question: What helps prevent drowsiness on long drives?
options: a:Slowing down and keeping a steady speed.,b:Drinking caffeinated beverages continuously.,c:Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.,d:Turning up the radio and keeping windows closed.
note: Schedule regular stops for rest and stretching to prevent drowsiness, even if you don't feel tired initially.

question: True or False: It is illegal to drive at night using only your parking lights.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking lights alone do not provide adequate illumination for night driving. You must use headlights when driving in the dark or when visibility is reduced.

question: A useful rule about passing is to:
options: a:Always try to reach the front of slow-moving traffic.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as necessary.,c:Pass anytime you are traveling faster than others.,d:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Passing increases collision risk; stay with the flow of traffic within legal limits and pass only when needed and safe."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal turns steady yellow as you approach and you have not yet entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Honk to warn cross traffic.,b:Proceed through at the same speed.,c:Come to a safe stop if you can do so.,d:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow means the light will turn red soon; if you can stop safely before the intersection, you should do so.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal signify?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.
note: A left arm extended downward is a hand signal indicating the driver intends to stop or slow down.

question: When a law enforcement officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment check, which document must you be able to produce?
options: a:Their license.,b:Proof of insurance.,c:Proof of registration.
note: Drivers are required to have and produce their operator's license when stopped; drivers are also responsible for providing proof of vehicle registration and insurance when requested.

question: What is the only thing that will reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Coffee and rest.,c:Exercise at moderate intensity.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC; remedies like coffee, food, or exercise do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed if you think it’s clear.,b:Stop and inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Honk to warn approaching traffic.,d:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.
note: If cross traffic is obscured, stop and inch forward slowly until you can see clearly both ways without entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Proceed to the next exit.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the missed exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next one. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median; those actions are dangerous and illegal.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:When the road is wet or slippery.,b:On narrow or winding roads.,c:At intersections or railroad crossings.
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding areas, near intersections or crossings, on hills and curves, where pedestrians are present, and when pavement is slippery.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should fit how?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is hidden beneath the seat.,c:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
note: Lap belts should lie across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should fit comfortably across the chest.

question: What colors do warning signs (for upcoming hazards) use?
options: a:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,b:White symbols on a blue background.,c:Black symbols on a white background.,d:White letters on brown background.
note: Standard warning signs use black symbols or lettering on a yellow background; work zone warnings use orange with black."

question: What do broken white lines on the roadway indicate?
options: a:They indicate two-way traffic.,b:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:They mark a no passing zone.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed with caution when changing lanes.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally until you find a service station.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, steer to keep control, and slow gradually before pulling off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you do just before moving?
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Check your rearview mirror.,c:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.
note: Before initiating the lane change, check mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to check blind spots for other vehicles.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, what action should you take immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn them.,b:Slowly inch forward to pass behind the child.,c:Turn on your parking lights and proceed cautiously.
note: If a child is about to enter the roadway and a collision is imminent, a sharp horn blast may warn them and help prevent an accident; always be prepared to brake.

question: What color are warning signs that specifically alert drivers to pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses?
options: a:Yellow-green,b:Blue,c:Brown,d:Red
note: Signs for pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, and school zones use a yellow-green background to increase visibility near areas with children.

question: What must you do when you approach a stopped school bus on your side of the road with red lights flashing?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and proceed cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass the bus carefully.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop until the lights stop flashing and the bus resumes motion or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limit or stop signs) are typically white with black or red markings and indicate laws or regulations that must be followed.

question: Double solid yellow lane markings indicate:
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is prohibited in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is it legal to make a left turn at a red light after stopping?
options: a:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,b:When traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street (unless a sign prohibits it).,c:Whenever traffic is light and it seems safe.
note: After a complete stop, you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, and only if no signs prohibit it and the way is clear.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,c:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
note: If an emergency vehicle is approaching, yield the right-of-way by pulling to the side or otherwise giving a clear lane when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road just before the exit lane.,b:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth up ahead.
note: Enter the exit lane in advance, then reduce speed after you are fully in the exit lane and follow posted advisory speeds.

question: Accumulating 12 points against your license in two years will result in automatic revocation for how many months?
options: a:Three,b:Six,c:Nine
note: Accumulating 12 violation points in a two-year period leads to automatic revocation of an operator's license for six months.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
options: a:Only in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if wearing reflective clothing.,c:Crossing any street in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,d:Only if they are in an intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks; for safety, yield to anyone crossing the street.

question: If a vehicle with high beams approaches you without dimming, where should you look?
options: a:Either side of the road equally.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,d:At the center of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining enough vision to stay on course."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How many feet before your turn should you signal?
options: a:150 feet,b:100 feet,c:50 feet
note: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes to give other drivers time to react to your intentions.

question: Braking distance is affected by which factor?
options: a:The condition of your brakes and tires.,b:The condition of the pavement.,c:The speed your vehicle is traveling.
note: Braking distance depends on vehicle speed, tire and brake condition, and roadway surface; higher speeds and poor conditions increase stopping distance.

question: Which statement about funeral procession escort vehicles is true?
options: a:They are not considered emergency vehicles.,b:They are emergency vehicles only when escorted by police.,c:They are classified as emergency vehicles.
note: Funeral escort vehicles displaying authorized signals are considered emergency vehicles and drivers should yield to them.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When being tailgated by another driver.,c:When driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If you are being tailgated, increase the gap in front of your vehicle to reduce the chance of a rear-end collision and avoid sudden braking.

question: To reduce glare from an oncoming vehicle's headlights, you should:
options: a:Flash your high beams at the oncoming driver.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on the centerline.,c:Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road and then refocus ahead.,d:Stare at the bright lights to adjust.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right side of the road briefly and then check ahead to maintain your lane position."

question: If another vehicle is in danger of hitting you, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,c:Turn off your headlights.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians to imminent danger; it is an immediate and effective warning signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When arriving at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: If vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in the appropriate order.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Is safe for drivers under 21.,b:Nearly doubles your chances of being involved in a fatal crash.,c:Has no effect on driving ability.,d:Is the legal limit for all drivers
note: Every 0.02% increase in BAC significantly increases the risk of a crash; even low BAC levels impair judgment and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must use your turn signal whenever you pull away from a curb to indicate your intention to other road users.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Turn off the engine.,c:Lock the ignition and remove the key.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Improve traffic flow.,b:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving so slowly that you hinder normal traffic flow can be unsafe and may result in a citation; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The vehicle in front moves slightly right.,b:The oncoming lane line is broken.,c:The broken yellow line is next to your lane.,d:There is a no passing sign
note: You may pass when the centerline next to your lane is broken, indicating passing is permitted from your direction when safe.

question: When passing a recently parked vehicle on the roadside, you should:
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Drive in the opposite lane to avoid it.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.,d:Assume the driver might open a door and use extra caution.
note: Expect that a person exiting or opening a door may step into the street; reduce speed and pass with caution."

question: Which action should you not omit when changing lanes?
options: a:Giving a turn signal.,b:Checking for other drivers who may also move into the same lane.,c:Driving faster than surrounding traffic.,d:Checking your side and rearview mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors, use your turn signal, and look for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

question: What message is shown on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:One-way,b:Do not enter,c:Stop
note: An octagonal red sign always means STOP; you must come to a complete stop at the sign.

question: When an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the vehicle’s wheels.,c:Directly at the lights to signal them,d:Toward the right side of the road.
note: Glancing toward the right side of the road will reduce glare and help you maintain your lane until the vehicle passes."

question: Are fines for speeding tripled in work and school zones?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In Nebraska fines for moving violations are typically doubled in work zones where workers are present and in designated school zones during restricted hours, not tripled.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Slow down,c:Stop immediately in your lane.,d:Speed up to avoid stopping in front of it.
note: When alerted to an emergency vehicle, slow down, move to give a clear path, and stop so the vehicle can pass safely.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates what?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline means drivers may cross the centerline to pass another vehicle on the left when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Left,c:Right
note: On roads without a curb, turn your wheels toward the side of the road (right) so if the vehicle rolls it will move away from traffic.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Check your mirrors frequently so you are aware of nearby traffic and can respond safely to changing conditions.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones are indicated by blue signs.,b:You do not need to slow down in work zones if workers are not present.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and be extra attentive.,d:Work zones are always stationary and marked with black and white signs.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., mowing or line-striping) and are identified by orange signs; slow down and pay extra attention when approaching or driving through them.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited from your lane because it would be unsafe to enter the opposing lane.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Speed up to beat cross traffic.,b:Ignore pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Proceed through the intersection if it is safe and clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go, but you must yield to vehicles or pedestrians still in the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning right on a solid red light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping,c:Come to a complete stop
note: Unless a sign prohibits it, a right turn on red is permitted only after you come to a complete stop and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that are not visible in mirrors; always glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: Which action is unlawful regarding a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and its stop arm extended?
options: a:Passing within 100 feet of any intersection.,b:Passing within 100 feet of any railroad crossing.,c:Passing the bus.
note: It is unlawful to pass a school bus that is stopped and displaying its flashing red lights with the stop arm extended. Drivers must stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion or the signals are turned off.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights are a good way to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Use only your instrument panel lights.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Use your low-beam headlights in reduced-visibility conditions (dawn, dusk, rain, snow) to help other drivers see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway across a sidewalk, what should drivers do?
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to your vehicle.,b:Proceed if no pedestrians are visible on the sidewalk.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.
note: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, stop before the sidewalk and yield to pedestrians and other traffic before entering the roadway.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams will reflect off the fog and reduce visibility; parking lights do not provide enough illumination for safe driving.

question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light indicates you may:
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the signal changes to green.,b:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn after you come to a complete stop.,d:Turn if no other vehicles are present
note: A red arrow means stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears; do not turn against a red arrow."

question: It is important to frequently check the traffic behind you when you are:
options: a:Slowing down.,b:Driving down steep hills.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Monitor traffic behind you regularly, especially before lane changes, slowing, backing up, or descending steep grades.

question: If you observe pedestrians in a crosswalk you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Continue; you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.,c:Pull to the right and go around them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: True or False: When driving in fog you should use high beam headlights to see better.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only on rural roads,d:Only if visibility is over 500 feet
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; in fog, use low beams or fog lights if equipped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line, you may:
options: a:Only cross during daylight,b:Only cross if you are in the left lane.,c:Cross the line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.,d:Not cross the line to pass.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes going the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe."

question: Vehicle stopping distances never depend on which factor?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle and brake condition, speed, road and weather conditions, and vehicle weight; it does not depend on the time of day.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution; it does not require a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with two or more lanes, how should you respond to a 'Merging traffic' sign?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Speed up to avoid congesting traffic.,c:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if possible.
note: When feasible and safe, move over one lane or adjust speed to allow merging vehicles to enter smoothly.

question: A good driver should monitor which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Stare directly in front of their car.,b:Watch beside,c:Only focus on the middle of the road.
note: Safe driving requires scanning ahead, to the sides, and behind to stay aware of changing traffic conditions and potential hazards.

question: True or False: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and must obey traffic laws.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Under Nebraska law, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists and must follow traffic laws; drivers should respect their right to share the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn who must you yield the right-of-way to?
options: a:Pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:Oncoming traffic.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and to any pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:Yellow and white,c:White
note: Yellow center lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Turning left on a red light is always prohibited.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Turning left on a red is permitted only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it; otherwise left turns on red are not allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing on the left, move back into the right lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:No passing is permitted from either lane.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane with the solid yellow line.,c:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.
note: When a broken yellow line is alongside a solid yellow line, drivers on the side with the broken line may pass when safe; drivers on the solid-side may not.

question: What happens to tires on a wet roadway as speed increases?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at clearing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: At higher speeds, tires become less effective at dispersing water and can lose contact with the road surface, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, you should:
options: a:Drive as you would under normal conditions.,b:Use your cruise control.,c:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
note: On snow or ice, make all speed and steering adjustments gradually; never use cruise control because it can reduce your ability to respond to loss of traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Never change lanes while you are in an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal your intentions before changing lanes.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection when it is safe to do so; yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Continue moving steadily and clear the intersection safely.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear the intersection safely rather than stopping suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what should you do after signaling?
options: a:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane,c:Merge carefully into the gap.
note: Identify a gap, match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge carefully when it is safe; do not assume other drivers will make room.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,b:At all times.,c:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and stop if necessary to allow them to cross safely.

question: When parked facing uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,d:Turn your wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll into the curb rather than into traffic.

question: How must a driver handle pedestrians, even if they are not following the rules?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.,b:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.,c:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers have a responsibility to avoid hitting pedestrians; yield to pedestrians whenever necessary to prevent a collision, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

question: When is pavement especially slippery during rain?
options: a:Just after rain begins because oil and dirt mix with water.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:Only when temperatures are below freezing.,d:When rain becomes a heavy downpour.
note: Roads are most treacherous shortly after rain starts because accumulated oil and dirt mix with water to create a slippery film."

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum BAC of:
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.08 percent.
note: Nebraska law prohibits operating a motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher for drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: Approach hills with caution and be prepared to stop for stalled vehicles or hazards you cannot yet see beyond the crest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street, you should start from which lane?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: Begin left turns from the far-left lane when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway?
options: a:Drive slowly so you can check traffic thoroughly.,b:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Signal
note: When merging onto a freeway, accelerate on the entrance ramp to match traffic speed, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the road.

question: What do broken yellow lines on the roadway indicate?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing may be allowed.,b:They mark no-passing zones.,c:They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
note: Yellow center lines separate opposite directions of traffic. A broken yellow line indicates passing is permitted when safe.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcyclists require a full lane to maneuver safely; never attempt to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for vehicles in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the side mirror on the side you plan to move to.,d:Signal without checking.
note: Glance over your shoulder toward the lane you will enter to check the blind spot; do this every time you change lanes."

question: Which of the following is not a safe interstate driving practice?
options: a:If you miss your exit, proceed to the next exit.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:Change lanes without signaling.
note: It is unsafe and illegal to change lanes without signaling. On interstates, use proper signals, keep right if slower, and take the next exit if you miss yours.

question: To ensure your physical condition does not impair driving, you should:
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Drive within your physical limitations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.
note: Be aware of health and medications that may affect your ability to operate a vehicle; drive only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into a driveway, alley, or private road.,b:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,c:At any time.
note: Solid yellow lines should not be crossed to pass. They may be crossed to make a left turn into or from a driveway, private road, or to enter/leave the roadway where permitted.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color background?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs (indicating laws and requirements) are usually white rectangles or squares with contrasting text or symbols.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, you must do what?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Cross the tracks at your own risk.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is approaching and could be dangerous, do not attempt to cross; wait until all tracks are clear before proceeding.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the one you want to enter is which type of line?
options: a:Solid yellow,b:Double solid yellow,c:Broken white
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: Pentagonal school crossing signs warn drivers to be alert for children and be prepared to slow or stop.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large and heavy vehicles need extra distance to stop; sudden stops can result in the larger vehicle being unable to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:If you increase your speed before the turn.,b:Only if a sign explicitly permits the turn.,c:If the traffic on the street you are turning onto is moving to the left.
note: You may turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street that has traffic moving to the left, unless prohibited by sign.

question: If you are involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Call the police.,c:Help the injured.
note: Stop immediately, move to safety if possible, and then call for emergency assistance and render aid without moving seriously injured persons unless necessary.

question: A steady green arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the arrow's direction and has the right-of-way.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green light and you may go straight or turn as you wish.,c:You may proceed in the arrow's direction only if a circular green light is also shown.,d:The arrow applies only on one-way streets.
note: A green arrow gives a protected movement in the arrow's direction; traffic in the indicated lane must turn that way while opposing traffic is stopped."

question: When must you use your headlights?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise (when visibility is reduced).,b:Only after 8 p.m. and before 7 a.m.,c:Between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m.
note: Headlights are required between sunset and sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced to about 500 feet or less (for example, in rain or fog).

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
note: Emotions affect driving performance; take time to calm down before operating a vehicle so you can concentrate on driving safely.

question: True or False: Drivers may park in handicap parking access aisles next to accessible stalls.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only with a permit,d:Only if loading a passenger
note: Parking in handicap access aisles is prohibited; these spaces provide room for wheelchair access and lifts and must remain clear."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, how should you signal a turn?
options: a:Use your horn.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Use hand signals.,d:Flash your brake lights rapidly.
note: If turn signals are inoperative, use recognized hand signals to indicate your intentions to other road users.

question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A steady red arrow,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left,d:A solid green light
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way to turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Traffic behind you only.,b:Only drivers signaling to exit the roundabout.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout; also watch for pedestrians and bicyclists at the approaches and crosswalks.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Safely pull to the curb and stop to check if it is on your street.,c:Keep driving until you spot the vehicle.,d:Continue at the same speed and look in your mirrors
note: If you hear a siren nearby but cannot locate the emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right and stop until you can determine its location and path.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, how should drivers respond?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using sirens or lights, pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until the vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Make room for the merging traffic,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When safe, adjust your speed or change lanes to allow merging vehicles to enter smoothly.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are more likely to use their headlights only during the day.,b:Motorcycles always travel much slower than cars.,c:Motorcyclists rarely follow traffic laws.,d:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss in traffic or in blind spots, and it's harder to judge their speed and distance, so exercise extra caution around them.

question: A driver license is considered:
options: a:A permanent entitlement,b:A guaranteed right.,c:An optional permit given to everyone.,d:A privilege that may be revoked for abuse.
note: Driving is a privilege that can be suspended or revoked if a driver abuses it; it is not an absolute right."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you cannot pass safely unless you:
options: a:Are able to clearly see the road ahead only.,b:Are in a hurry.,c:Can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic and can clearly see the road ahead.,d:Have a vehicle capable of high speed only.
note: Safe passing requires clear sight of the road ahead, the ability to return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic, and sufficient vehicle capability to complete the pass safely.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Try to drive through the crossing quickly.,b:Maintain your speed and ignore warning signs.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When you approach a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If lights are flashing or gates are down, stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks and do not go around the gate.

question: What is a major cause of rear-end collisions in work zones?
options: a:Construction equipment obstructing drivers' views.,b:The lack of work zone barricades.,c:Driving at a different speed than surrounding traffic.
note: Rear-end collisions in work zones often occur when drivers travel at different speeds than neighboring traffic; maintain consistent speeds and pay attention to posted limits.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard and hold them down.,b:Turn on hazard lights and coast to a stop in the lane.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly,d:Pull over immediately without braking.
note: Keep the vehicle going straight, gradually slow by easing off the gas and using light braking, then pull safely off the road.

question: Why must you use greater caution when driving at night?
options: a:Traffic volume is always higher at night.,b:Vehicles stop more quickly at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
note: Reduced lighting at night limits visibility; therefore you must slow down, increase following distance, and use headlights appropriately between sunset and sunrise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed if the road looks clear.
note: A red light means you must stop. Stop at the stop line, and if there is no line, stop before entering any crosswalk or the intersection itself.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or other conditions of reduced visibility; high beams will reflect back and reduce your visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Using a handheld wireless device to read, type, or send written communication while driving is what type of offense?
options: a:As a radio.,b:As a GPS navigation device.,c:To read
note: In Nebraska it is a secondary offense to use a handheld device to read, type, or send written communications while driving; fines may apply.

question: You should allow extra following distance when you are:
options: a:When following a small passenger car.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: Give extra space when following large vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers) because they may not see you and can block your view ahead.

question: After overtaking another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:As soon as you signal.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and you have checked blind spots."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for changing lanes?
options: a:Signal and move lanes immediately without checking mirrors.,b:Signal,c:Check your mirrors
note: Before changing lanes, signal your intention, check side and rearview mirrors, then glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.,c:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.
note: When parked on a hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park or in gear; turn wheels as recommended depending on curb presence and direction of slope.

question: When traveling through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Stop to watch the workers if traffic is slow.,b:Decrease your following distance to clear the area quickly.,c:Pass carefully and avoid slowing to stare at the scene ('rubbernecking').
note: Stay focused, obey signs and flaggers, and do not slow unnecessarily to look at the work site; rubbernecking can create additional hazards and delays.

question: What does the term for the amount of alcohol in the blood refer to?
options: a:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,b:Alcohol absorption index (AAI).,c:Implied consent (IC).,d:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in a person’s bloodstream; higher BAC indicates greater impairment."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on the interstate, slower-moving traffic should:
options: a:Drive with four-way flashers activated.,b:Stay in the left lane at all times.,c:Keep to the right.
note: On multi-lane highways and interstates, slower traffic should keep to the right so faster vehicles can use left lanes to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or without warning.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes abruptly or without signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots. Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.

question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, what should you confirm?
options: a:You have sounded your horn to signal your return.,b:You have flashed your lights to warn the other driver.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, check your rearview mirror and make sure you can see the passed vehicle's headlights before merging back into the lane to ensure a safe gap.

question: If drivers keep passing you on both sides while you're in the expressway center lane, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match traffic.,b:Move into the lane to your right.,c:Move into the lane to your left.,d:Stay in the center lane.
note: On multi-lane roads with two-way traffic, stay in the right lanes unless passing or preparing to turn left. On interstates, slower drivers should use the right lane so faster traffic can pass.

question: Interstate driving requires which of the following?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,c:Be constantly alert.
note: Safe interstate driving requires both the ability to handle higher speeds and constant alertness to rapidly changing conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a business district?
options: a:30 miles per hour.,b:20 miles per hour.,c:25 miles per hour.
note: The usual speed limit in a business district is 20 mph unless another limit is posted. Always obey posted speed signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven under what conditions?
options: a:During the night.,b:Under ideal conditions.,c:During the day.
note: The posted speed limit represents the maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions; drivers should slow down when conditions are worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum legal speed on Nebraska interstate highways under normal conditions?
options: a:50 mph.,b:60 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: The minimum posted speed on many Nebraska interstates is 40 mph; drive no slower than posted minimums unless road or weather conditions require slower speeds.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because other drivers will pull in front of you to pass the large vehicle.,b:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream and save fuel.,c:To see around the sides of the vehicle and have more time to react.
note: Large vehicles can block your view of the road ahead and require longer stopping distances; increasing your following distance improves visibility and safety.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,b:Turn up the radio and open the windows.,c:Increase your speed to finish sooner.
note: If you experience drowsiness or signs of fatigue (such as drifting lanes or heavy eyes), stop in a safe place and rest or take a short nap; stimulation methods do not replace sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, who must you yield to?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Yield the right-of-way to any oncoming traffic and to pedestrians before completing a left turn when required by signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield to motorists who arrived before them.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrived first has the right-of-way; vehicles proceed in the order of arrival.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain speed and steer aggressively to regain control.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop as quickly as possible.,c:Steer straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, avoid heavy braking until the vehicle is under control, and then slow and pull off the road safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the normal speed limit in a residential district?
options: a:20 miles per hour.,b:30 miles per hour.,c:25 miles per hour.
note: The typical residential speed limit is 25 mph unless signs indicate a different limit. Always obey posted signage.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop whether or not children are present.,b:Sound your horn to warn students.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: Approach school crossing signs with caution, watch for children, and be prepared to stop; only stop when necessary for pedestrians or when signs indicate.

question: What can help you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the vehicle in front of you to show displeasure.,b:Relax and focus on safe driving.,c:Drive faster to get past slow traffic.
note: Stay calm, plan extra travel time, obey speed limits, and avoid taking other drivers' actions personally to prevent aggressive driving behavior.

question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will:
options: a:Significantly increase your chances of being involved in a crash.,b:Not significantly increase your chances of being involved in a crash.
note: Using a phone while driving is a serious distraction that substantially raises the risk of crashing.

question: All children under age 18 in Nebraska are required to:
options: a:Ride in the front seat only.,b:Wear only lap belts,c:Always sit in the back seat.,d:Be secured in a safety belt or child safety seat.
note: Nebraska law requires that all passengers under 18 be properly restrained in a seat belt or child safety seat when riding in a moving vehicle."

question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, what is required?
options: a:May not proceed until it changes to green.,b:Treat the intersection as if it were controlled by a stop sign.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Your speed does not affect the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at night,d:Only at high speeds
note: Higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance; as speed rises, the distance needed to stop also increases.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:When pulling next to,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Signal before pulling up to the curb and before pulling away so other road users know your intentions.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, what is the recommended braking technique?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: If a tire suddenly goes flat, hold the steering wheel, steer straight, ease off the gas, and apply the brakes lightly as you slow and pull off the roadway.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, the first action to take is to:
options: a:Shift into neutral.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,d:Apply the parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, first remove pressure from the accelerator; apply gentle, steady braking only if more deceleration is needed.

question: If poor weather sharply reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When visibility or conditions worsen, increase following distance to give yourself more time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull as far to the right as possible without leaving the pavement.,b:Stay in your lane and reduce your speed.,c:Stay in your lane and maintain your speed unless there is an emergency.
note: When being passed, stay in your lane and maintain speed. Only take evasive action if necessary to avoid a collision.

question: May you drive around lowered crossing gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing.,b:When the train has passed.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must never go around a lowered railroad crossing gate—stop and wait until it is fully raised and the way is clear.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:To test a vehicle’s shock absorbers.,b:To slow traffic with a rough surface.,c:To alert inattentive drivers by vibration and sound that they have left the travel lane or are approaching a hazard.,d:To inform drivers of tire pressure problems.
note: Rumble strips produce vibration and sound to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the lane or approaching a stop or hazard."

question: Is it safe to use cruise control while driving on snowy or icy roads if you reduce speed?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads; it can reduce your ability to react and regain control if you start to skid or hydroplane.

question: Which of the following is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Maintain the same speed throughout the curve.,b:Speed up as you enter the curve to maintain momentum.,c:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and accelerate gently as you exit to maintain traction and control; increasing speed entering a curve makes control more difficult.

question: When lanes are separated by double solid yellow lines, what is allowed?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the right.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited from both directions because it is unsafe to cross into the oncoming lane.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Walk into the road to attract drivers' attention.
note: If stranded, remain in your vehicle, keep warm, and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle.

question: Children up to what age are prohibited from riding in cargo areas of vehicles?
options: a:12 years old.,b:18 years old.,c:10 years old.
note: Nebraska law prohibits children under 18 from riding in cargo areas; children must be properly restrained in seats or safety belts while the vehicle is moving.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window and turning on the radio will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they may appear intoxicated.,c:Drinking strong coffee will immediately restore full driving ability.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving to the extent that drivers may appear to be intoxicated; simple measures like opening a window or radio are insufficient to ensure safety.

question: In Nebraska, the BAC limit for drivers under age 21 is:
options: a:0.1 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.
note: Drivers under 21 are subject to a lower BAC limit (0.02%) under Nebraska's zero-tolerance laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Drivers may pass on a two-lane roadway marked with a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
options: a:True,b:Only during daylight,c:Only with turn signals,d:False
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited; passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line."

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Take some caffeine pills.,b:Take a break.,c:Try to fight it.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop at the first safe location to rest, change drivers, or take a short nap—caffeine and other quick fixes are not substitutes for rest.

question: True or False: A motorist making a left turn must yield to a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction.
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles in the same way you would yield to oncoming motor vehicles; proceed only when it is safe.

question: True or False: Motorists are not required to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic signal.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians even if they cross against a signal; always be alert and prepared to stop for pedestrians.

question: What does a steady red arrow indicate to drivers?
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction without stopping.,b:Drivers cannot proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after stopping.
note: A steady red arrow means vehicles in the indicated lane may not proceed in that direction until the arrow changes to a green signal.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A reflective orange triangular emblem
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle; it indicates a vehicle traveling 25 mph or less."

question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Maintain normal speed.,b:Yield only to pedestrians.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Come to a complete stop every time.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution after slowing; it does not require a complete stop unless directed by other signs or signals."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop regardless of other traffic.,b:Maintain speed and proceed unless another vehicle honks.,c:Yield to traffic approaching from the right and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, slow down, cover the brake, and yield to vehicles on your right; be ready to stop to avoid conflicts.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, then proceed.,c:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.,d:Treat it the same as a red light.
note: A flashing yellow warns of a hazard — slow down and proceed with caution but you do not have to stop."

question: Is it lawful to operate a motor vehicle with a television screen visible to the driver?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Nebraska law prohibits operating a motor vehicle when the vehicle is equipped with a television or video screen visible to the driver.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
note: At multi-track crossings, wait until you have a clear view of all tracks and are sure no other trains are approaching before crossing.

question: By law, how much lateral space must motorists leave when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Two feet,b:One foot,c:Three feet,d:No set distance
note: Nebraska law requires motorists to provide at least three feet of clearance when passing a bicycle and to maintain that space until safely past the bicyclist."

question: When driving at night, what should you do to drive more safely?
options: a:Always use high beams regardless of other vehicles.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Look directly into oncoming headlights.,d:Follow the taillights of the car ahead closely.
note: Increase following distance at night to allow more time to react; use proper high/low beam technique and avoid staring into oncoming lights."

question: Construction zone signs typically have what shape and colors?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.,b:Square with white and red coloring.,c:Round with black and yellow coloring.,d:Pentagonal with yellow-green background
note: Temporary work zone signs are orange with black lettering or symbols and are often diamond-shaped or rectangular."

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Drive more slowly than usual.,c:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.
note: Allow at least a three- to four-second following distance behind motorcycles, since they can stop more quickly and are more vulnerable.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, which response is safest?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up.
note: Safest practice is to avoid confrontation—move aside, change lanes, or let the aggressive driver pass.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Trucks require a smaller turning radius than cars.,c:Trucks always travel slower than passenger cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need longer stopping distances and require extra room when turning. Allow trucks more space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:
