options: a:Enter the circle without yielding,b:Yield to traffic already within the roundabout.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout; traffic moves counterclockwise and approaches from your left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped at a red light that displays a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait until the light changes.
note: A green arrow allows traffic in the indicated lane to proceed in that direction when the way is clear; yield to any pedestrians or traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, what is the general rule for who goes first?
options: a:The driver who arrives first proceeds first.,b:Drivers may insist on the right-of-way even if unsafe.,c:Drivers should always yield to vehicles on the left.
note: Vehicles should proceed through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, vehicles are entering from an entrance ramp on your right. What should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane.,b:Merge left to give them space for a smooth,c:Increase your speed to try to beat the merging vehicles.
note: When traffic is merging onto the interstate from an on-ramp to your right, signal and move left when it is safe to create a gap for a smooth, safe entry. If you cannot move left safely, adjust your speed to help the incoming vehicles merge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: It is legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle.
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must obey the posted speed limit at all times; exceeding it to pass is illegal and unsafe.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use which lights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams will reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: True or False: You may never drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier.
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to go around or under lowered railroad crossing gates or barriers; always wait until gates are fully raised and signals stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,b:One driver should continue driving without stopping.,c:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has priority.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic but your light is green, you should:
options: a:Follow the vehicle ahead into the intersection.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Turn left to find another route immediately.,d:Stop in the intersection and wait
note: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot clear it; blocking the intersection can impede cross traffic and may result in a ticket."

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink black coffee to sober up quickly.,b:Take a brisk walk to burn off alcohol.,c:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time decreases BAC; stimulants or activities cannot remove alcohol from your bloodstream or sober you up.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Both of the above.,c:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.
note: In work zones, do not follow too closely and be attentive for workers and construction equipment. Both tailgating and inattention increase the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:You wait until the light changes.,b:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,c:You first come to a complete stop.
note: A green arrow indicates you may proceed in that direction from the appropriate lane when the way is clear; yield to any pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the intersection.,b:Yield just to the traffic on the right.,c:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the roadway you are entering.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop only if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only on hills.,c:Only in school zones.,d:Only at night
note: It's unsafe and illegal to pass on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility is limited or hazards exist.

question: When parking facing uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Leave the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls it will move away from traffic and rest against the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Slow down dramatically and drift into the lane.,b:Only glance at the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, check side mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; confirm the lane is clear and signal before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often leads to what?
options: a:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:Does not increase the chance of a crash.
note: Driving at excessive speeds reduces reaction time and often results in poor decision-making that contributes to crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A speed limit denotes what?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.,c:The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (or minimum where posted) legal speed under ideal conditions; reduce speed when conditions are unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the right lane of the one-way street.,c:In the center of the street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane of that one-way street, closest to the lane you came from.

question: An orange and red triangular sign mounted on the back of a vehicle means what?
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: An orange and red reflective triangle identifies a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or road maintenance vehicles.

question: When approaching snow removal equipment on the roadway, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Follow closely to pass quickly.,b:Maintain at least 100 feet of following distance.,c:Drive alongside the equipment until it turns off the roadway.
note: Keep a safe distance—about 100 feet—behind snowplows or other maintenance vehicles to avoid reduced visibility from blowing snow or flying debris and to reduce the chance of collision.

question: What should you do with your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Keep your speed exactly the same.,b:Reduce your speed to a controllable level.,c:Brake hard during the turn.,d:Increase your speed to maintain momentum.
note: Slow to a speed that allows you to maintain control of your vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected hazards when turning.

question: Nebraska law requires reporting a crash within how many days if there is injury, death, or apparent damages exceeding a dollar amount?
options: a:Five days / $250,b:10 days / $1,000,c:15 days / $750
note: You must report a crash to the Department of Roads within 10 days if it caused injury or death or if it appears to have caused more than $1,000 in property damage.

question: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones are commonly used to guide drivers through work zones. True or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Work zones commonly use barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones to guide traffic; drivers should pass through work zones with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, when should you go?
options: a:Immediately,b:After coming to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Only when there is an adequate gap in circulating traffic.
note: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout and enter only when there is a safe gap.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Activate your four-way flashers.,b:Increase your speed so as not to impede traffic.,c:Stay alert
note: In work zones, remain alert, follow posted directions, adjust your speed to conditions, and be prepared to stop suddenly to protect workers and other motorists.

question: What are the penalties for failing to secure child passengers properly?
options: a:No penalty for first offense,b:Two points plus court costs.,c:Two points assessed against the driver.,d:A fine and one point assessed against the driver.
note: Drivers cited for not securing child passengers may face a fine (typically $25 plus court costs) and one point on their driving record."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,b:Go to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not working and no officer is present, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop.,b:Allow traffic on major streets to proceed without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by yield signs.
note: When traffic signals are not working and no officer is directing traffic, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: stop, then proceed when the way is clear.

question: What may occur if alcohol is taken together with another drug?
options: a:Both effects will always be reduced.,b:Both will cancel out and produce no effect.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
note: Alcohol combined with other drugs can intensify the impairing effects of each, leading to greater impairment than when using either substance alone.

question: Which of these is a place you should never park?
options: a:In a designated handicap space when you have a permit.,b:On a hill with a curb and set parking brake.,c:In front of a public or private driveway.
note: It is illegal to park in front of private or public driveways. Other prohibited places include within 20 feet of a crosswalk and within 30 feet of many traffic-control devices unless otherwise posted.

question: Blue-colored traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance zones.,b:Motorist services such as rest areas,c:Mileage distances to cities only.,d:Regulatory requirements.
note: Blue roadway signs are service signs giving information about available motorist services like rest areas, gas, food, and hospitals.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:The same as daytime driving.,b:Legal only on major roads.,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and more impaired or tired drivers may be on the road.,d:Less dangerous due to lighter traffic.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from headlights, and a higher likelihood of tired or impaired drivers.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Drivers of small vehicles cannot see trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses usually travel faster than passenger cars.,c:Large trucks and buses have air brakes and cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.
note: Large commercial vehicles use air brakes, which take longer to activate than hydraulic brakes on passenger vehicles; therefore trucks and buses cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.

question: What must you do when a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow the surrounding traffic.,b:Follow the flagger's directions.,c:Assume the flagger is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: When a flagger controls traffic in a work zone, obey their signals and directions for the safety of workers and drivers; failing to do so is illegal and dangerous.

question: When vehicles are merging from on-ramps to your right on an interstate, the best action to avoid conflict is to:
options: a:Move to the right lane and slow significantly.,b:Maintain your current speed and lane.,c:Brake sharply to let them in.,d:Change lanes to the left when traffic allows.
note: If safe, move out of the right-hand lane to allow merging traffic from on-ramps to enter the freeway smoothly.

question: If you pass a stopped emergency or road assistance vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do if possible?
options: a:Move into a lane at least one travel lane away from the stopped vehicle, if possible.,b:Stop.,c:Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle.
note: When practical and legal, move at least one lane over away from stopped emergency or maintenance vehicles using flashing lights; otherwise slow down and pass with care.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and ensure there is room to clear the tracks.
note: When there are no flashing lights or gates, look and listen for trains, be prepared to yield, and never cross unless you can completely clear the tracks on the far side.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Come to a stop.,c:Turn right.
note: The hand signal of the left arm extended upward indicates the driver intends to turn right. Be aware of this when following or passing.

question: What color are temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Orange.
note: Work zone and temporary construction signs have orange backgrounds with black lettering or symbols to alert drivers to changes and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to a driver who:
options: a:Arrived before you,b:Is across from you,c:Is on your left,d:Is turning left
note: At intersections with stop signs on all corners, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive; yield to any driver who arrived before you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no-passing zone or within the prohibited distances of crossings and intersections.,b:Passing more than one vehicle at a time.,c:Passing on multilane highways.,d:Passing only during daylight
note: Passing is illegal in no-passing zones and within specified distances of railroad crossings and intersections; observe posted restrictions."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed through at the same speed.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Make a sudden lane change.,d:Prepare to stop safely and do so if possible.
note: A steady yellow indicates the signal will turn red soon; if you can stop safely before the intersection, do so.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Does not affect driving ability.,b:Is a distracting activity that can take your hands or attention off the wheel.,c:Is only prohibited for new drivers,d:Is recommended to stay alert.
note: Lighting or preparing to smoke distracts you by taking hands and eyes off driving tasks and increases crash risk."

question: When riding in a vehicle, which is the correct requirement for small children?
options: a:They should be secured in an appropriate child safety seat.,b:They are safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:They may be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Children who are too small for regular seat belts must be properly secured in a federally-approved child safety seat; holding a child is not safe.

question: What do flashing arrow panels in work zones typically indicate?
options: a:They are only used on interstate highways.,b:They guide drivers into certain lanes and indicate that part of the roadway is closed.,c:They direct drivers to stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: Flashing arrow panels are used in work zones to direct traffic into specific lanes and to warn that a lane or section of roadway is closed ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Never in parking lots.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or driveway to communicate your intentions to other road users.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, what should you do before exiting the vehicle?
options: a:Leave the vehicle running and exit immediately.,b:Shift to park and set the parking brake.,c:Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
note: After signaling and pulling off the road, shift into park, set the parking brake, activate emergency flashers, turn off the engine, and remove the keys before exiting if it is safe to do so.

question: If the roadway ahead is filled with heavy smoke, what action should you take?
options: a:Slow, move far right, and stop off the roadway until it is safe to continue.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue slowly.,c:Turn on your high beams and proceed cautiously.,d:Make a U-turn immediately.
note: If heavy smoke covers the road, reduce speed, pull as far right as possible, stop off the roadway, and determine whether it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.,b:Only after signaling for at least 10 seconds.,c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: After completing a pass, return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle entirely in your rearview mirror and you have enough space to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Low speeds,c:Driving at night only,d:Driving on smooth roads
note: Higher speeds lead to much longer stopping distances and increase the energy and severity involved in collisions."

question: Combining alcohol with drugs can have what effect?
options: a:Help cure your illness.,b:Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,c:Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
note: In many cases, alcohol and drugs can amplify each other’s effects, making driving much more dangerous than using either substance alone.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Fall farther back than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow more closely to reduce wind drag on your car.,c:Drive on the truck's right side and wait to pass.
note: Large vehicles have greater stopping distances and larger blind spots; leave extra following distance so you can see around the truck and allow it time to stop.

question: The impairment caused by severe lack of sleep is most similar to which of these?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that alcohol has.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue can impair driving much like alcohol. For example, being awake 18 hours can impair driving similar to a BAC of about 0.05%; 24 hours awake is similar to about 0.10%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you can maintain control; avoid heavy braking while turning.

question: Drivers in Nebraska who refuse chemical testing when requested face a license suspension of:
options: a:One year,b:30 days,c:90 days,d:Six months
note: Under Nebraska’s Implied Consent Law, refusal to submit to chemical testing when requested by an officer can result in administrative license revocation for one year.

question: When driving in icy or snowy conditions, which technique is most effective at preventing crashes?
options: a:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,b:Get off the highway as quickly as possible regardless of route.,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance (avoid abrupt maneuvers).
note: Reducing speed, increasing following distance, and making smooth, deliberate maneuvers are the most effective ways to reduce crash risk on snow- or ice-covered roads.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are likely blind or visually impaired.,b:They may be deaf.,c:They may be a police officer.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a pedestrian is blind or visually impaired; slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop.

question: As you approach an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Only proceed on a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and be cautious; check for cross traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?
options: a:If you are under the BAC legal limit,b:Coffee can sober you up quickly.,c:Alcohol impairs judgment,d:If you can walk a straight line you are safe to drive.
note: Alcohol affects judgment and decision-making necessary for safe driving; impairment can occur even below legal BAC limits."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You signal your intention for three seconds.
note: You may safely return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror and you have enough space.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct procedure to return to the road?
options: a:Turn sharply to get back onto the pavement as quickly as possible.,b:Stop immediately and wait for assistance.,c:Reduce speed
note: If you leave the pavement, slow down gradually, check for traffic, and carefully steer back onto the roadway when it is safe to do so to avoid losing control.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirements as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and yielding to any right-of-way traffic, just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you begin to reduce speed?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain your highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the advisory speed posted for the exit ramp.

question: Never park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:Five feet,b:10 feet,c:15 feet
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited; always park only where it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Merge into the next lane when possible.,c:Speed up to leave a gap for them.
note: When it is safe, change lanes to create space for entering traffic. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to allow the vehicles to merge smoothly.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed normally.,b:Speed up.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians with visual or mobility impairments and be prepared to stop for their safety.

question: The most common mistake drivers make while backing is:
options: a:Failing to look both ways behind them.,b:Using the mirrors correctly.,c:Backing slowly.
note: Drivers often rely too much on mirrors when reversing; turning to look through the rear window gives a better view and reduces backup collisions.

question: Within how many days must you apply for a replacement operator's license after changing your name or address?
options: a:90 days.,b:10 days.,c:60 days.
note: If your name changes you must apply at a Driver Licensing Office; if your address changes you must update it online or at a Driver Licensing Office within 60 days of the change.

question: Which of the following is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper turning lanes on some highways?
options: a:Arrows and lane markings painted or signed to indicate lane purposes.,b:Flashing red lights,c:Flashing yellow lights
note: Arrows—on signs, overhead displays, or pavement—along with lane markings, are used to guide drivers into lanes designated for turns or through traffic.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations.,b:Warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,c:Directions to cities and towns ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow and black signs are warning signs that alert drivers to road conditions or hazards ahead.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle if space allows.,b:Expect the motorcycle to use only half a lane so you can share it.,c:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and do not share lanes.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane of travel. Do not share a lane with a motorcycle; give motorcyclists the same space and respect as other vehicles.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Brake suddenly to discourage passing,c:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle for them to complete the pass.,d:Maintain your speed and ignore them.
note: Slow slightly to increase the gap in front of you so the other driver can pass more easily and safely."

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Only if you are stopped and cited.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are involved in a collision.
note: You must carry evidence of financial responsibility and show proof of insurance and your license to an officer when requested after a traffic stop or collision.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning in heavy rain, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to reduce the chance of hydroplaning; do not use cruise control in heavy rain.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lights?
options: a:Drive using your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights (low beam).,c:Not turn on any vehicle lights.
note: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights and use low beams within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or 500 feet when following another vehicle.

question: What penalties might result from fleeing to avoid arrest?
options: a:The driver can be charged with a misdemeanor or felony offense.,b:The driver could have their operator's license revoked.,c:Both of the above.
note: Attempting to flee from law enforcement can result in misdemeanor or felony charges depending on the offense, and the driver’s license may be revoked.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A stop requirement.,b:A regulatory instruction.,c:A school zone or school crossing.,d:A railroad crossing.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is typically used to mark school zones or school crossings where children may be present."

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Parking on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes is illegal; follow posted rules and park within the allowed area and distance from the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,b:When they are on a road to your left and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When entering a street from a garage
note: You must yield when entering a roadway from a garage, alley, private driveway, or sidewalk and to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

question: Is failing to secure children under age six in a federally-approved child safety seat a traffic violation punishable by a $25 fine and one point?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nebraska law requires children up to age six to be secured in approved child safety seats; violation carries a fine and one point on the driver's record.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Eating,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.
note: Any secondary task—such as using a phone, eating, or adjusting audio—diverts attention from driving and increases crash risk.

question: In rainy weather, when are turning and stopping most hazardous?
options: a:During the first half hour of rainfall.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery during the first 10 to 30 minutes of rain because oils on the pavement mix with water, creating a slick surface.

question: On a green arrow, what must drivers do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,b:Proceed without yielding because the arrow gives you the right-of-way.,c:Yield to any vehicle
note: A green arrow means you may go, but you must first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Nebraska's speed law require of drivers?
options: a:Drive at a speed that is reasonable and safe for current conditions, within posted limits.,b:Always drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Drive five miles per hour over the posted limit to keep traffic flowing.
note: Nebraska law requires drivers to go at a safe and reasonable speed for existing conditions, not simply at the posted limit if conditions (weather, traffic, visibility) make that unsafe.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Immediately slam on the brakes.,b:Continue driving to the nearest service station.,c:Take your foot off the gas and do not immediately apply the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the accelerator, do not brake hard immediately, keep the vehicle straight, and gradually slow before pulling off the roadway.

question: If you plan to drink socially, which of these is a safe way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving while impaired; coffee or a cold shower do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or impairment.

question: Approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign with no painted crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: a:Before entering the unmarked crosswalk.,b:Inside the unmarked crosswalk.,c:At the stop sign regardless of crosswalk position.
note: Stop before entering the unmarked crosswalk (if present) or before the intersection; never stop in the crosswalk area.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow at any time.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow indicates the protected turning period is ending and has the same meaning as a circular yellow light: slow down and prepare to stop if you cannot safely clear the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to allow the passing vehicle to return safely to the travel lane.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Pull off the road.
note: If you are being passed, slow down as necessary to let the passing vehicle move back into the drive lane safely and as soon as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has more than one lane going your direction, which lane should you turn into?
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, complete the turn into the lane nearest your original lane and remain in that lane.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection means:
options: a:Continue at the posted speed without changing behavior.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for green.,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing yellow warns drivers to approach with caution, slow down, and proceed when safe.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Safety belts used properly and airbags together provide the most protection in frontal crashes; always buckle up even if your vehicle has airbags.

question: A round sign is used to indicate what ahead?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing; approach with caution and be prepared to stop.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.,c:Work hard to steer
note: Lose of power steering makes steering heavier; reduce speed, steer carefully to a safe place, and stop to fix the problem.

question: True or False: A motorist convicted of evading arrest for violating Nebraska law can have their driver license revoked.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Attempting to avoid arrest by fleeing law enforcement may result in driver license revocation under Nebraska law.

question: Except when passing, how close should you follow a working snow removal vehicle?
options: a:500 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet
note: Do not follow snow removal or maintenance equipment closer than 100 feet except when passing. These vehicles can create clouds of blowing snow and may throw ice or debris.

question: A sign reading “Reduced speed, 35 mph” means:
options: a:You have extra distance to slow before the reduced zone begins.,b:The reduced speed begins at the next posted sign.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,d:It is only advisory and not enforceable.
note: When a reduced speed is posted on a sign, the new legally enforceable speed limit begins at that sign.

question: Why is driving too slowly sometimes dangerous?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic can increase the risk of collisions, as other drivers may make risky maneuvers to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when parking.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Never; mirrors are sufficient.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to check blind spots whenever you change lanes, turn, or pull toward or away from a curb.

question: True or False: When completing an emergency roadside stop, it is not necessary to set the parking brake.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only on flat ground,d:Only if on the shoulder
note: Always set the parking brake during an emergency roadside stop to help keep your vehicle secure; also use emergency flashers to alert other drivers."

question: When does stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways only.,c:Only when driving at night.,d:When using cruise control.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose surfaces as well as when driving at higher speeds.

question: If a crash causes no injuries and only minor damage, what should drivers typically do with their vehicles?
options: a:Turn vehicles off and leave them in the middle of the roadway.,b:Leave vehicles where they were impacted and wait for police to move them.,c:Drive the vehicles out of travel lanes and onto the nearest shoulder.
note: If possible, move vehicles from travel lanes to the shoulder to avoid creating traffic hazards; if a vehicle cannot be moved, use hazard signals and call for assistance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates what?
options: a:Only a recommended driving speed.,b:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers should slow down when conditions are less than ideal.

question: Regarding vehicles equipped with airbags, which statement is correct?
options: a:A safety belt should not be worn by the driver of a vehicle equipped with airbags.,b:Children age 12 and under can safely sit in the front seat of a car that is equipped with airbags.,c:When combined with safety belts
note: Airbags are supplemental to seat belts and provide additional protection; children age 12 and under should sit in the rear seat whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you legally follow a fire apparatus responding to an emergency?
options: a:You may follow as close as needed to clear the way.,b:You must not follow closer than 100 feet.,c:You must not follow closer than 500 feet.
note: Do not follow emergency vehicles responding to calls within 500 feet; also avoid parking within a block of where a fire apparatus has stopped to answer an emergency.

question: What color and text combination do temporary work zone signs use?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary construction and maintenance signs use orange backgrounds with black lettering or symbols to call attention to work areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is one of the main dangers of excessive speed?
options: a:It saves significant travel time on short trips.,b:It helps you maneuver around obstacles more safely.,c:It increases the likelihood of serious injury or death in a crash.
note: Excessive speed reduces the time you have to react, increases stopping distance, and raises the severity of crashes, often causing serious injury or death.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Immediately turn off the ignition while still moving at speed.,b:Pump the accelerator pedal to free it.,c:Turn on your four-way hazard flashers
note: If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral, activate your emergency flashers, apply the brakes to slow, and safely steer the vehicle off the road before shutting off the engine; avoid turning off the ignition while moving fast to prevent loss of power steering.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles are always slower than cars.,b:They do not follow traffic rules.,c:Motorcycles can stop much faster than standard vehicles,d:Motorcyclists do not signal.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver quickly; following too closely reduces your time to react and increases crash risk."

question: Which practice best ensures safety when you are backing up your vehicle?
options: a:Sound your horn just before shifting into reverse.,b:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check for obstacles before getting in.,c:Rely solely on rearview mirrors while backing.
note: Before backing, get out and check behind your vehicle for children, small objects, or other hazards. Mirrors and cameras can help, but a visual walk-around is safest.

question: If a transit bus signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Race past the bus before it merges.,b:Honk to let the driver know you see them.,c:Ignore the signal.,d:Yield to the bus and allow it to merge.
note: You must yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter the roadway after loading/unloading; change lanes or slow to let them in safely."

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn repeatedly and proceed.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if no crosswalk is present. Stop and let the person safely complete crossing.

question: Why should you avoid using high-beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:They cause vehicles behind you to follow too closely.,b:They make it harder for approaching vehicles to see you.,c:High beams reflect the light back into your eyes and reduce visibility.
note: High beams reflect off fog, mist, or heavy precipitation and create glare that reduces your ability to see the road; use low beams instead.

question: Which of the following helps a person overcome the influence of alcohol?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime,b:Hot coffee,c:The passage of time
note: Only time will allow the body to metabolize alcohol and eliminate its effects; food, coffee, or fresh air do not speed this process.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after stopping you should look in which sequence before proceeding?
options: a:Check only the rearview mirror before moving.,b:Look left only and proceed.,c:Look right first
note: When stopped at an intersection, glance right, then left, and right again to ensure you have not missed approaching vehicles or pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: There may be times when driving 10 mph is too fast. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must reduce speed below the posted limit when road, traffic, or visibility conditions make it unsafe to travel at that speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly then turn.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Swing wide to the right before turning.,d:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and only turn when it is safe to do so."

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Open a window.,c:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: The safest response to drowsiness is to stop driving and rest or switch drivers; quick fixes like coffee or windows won’t replace sleep.

question: How should railroad crossings always be regarded?
options: a:Dangerous.,b:Safe places to stop and park.,c:Safe to cross in most situations.
note: Railroad crossings can be dangerous; always look and listen for trains and obey warning devices and signs.

question: What is required of drivers at a crosswalk?
options: a:Construction workers have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must always yield to vehicles.,c:You must yield to pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks; drivers must yield to them whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked, unless a traffic control device indicates otherwise.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red.,b:Ignore it and maintain current speed.,c:Slow and prepare to stop unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely; do not accelerate to beat the red light.

question: If a pedestrian entered the crosswalk after the 'Don't Walk' started flashing and is still in the street when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,b:Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding.,c:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian still in the crosswalk even if your light turns green; wait until they finish crossing before proceeding.

question: If other drivers are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact.,b:Don't react with hand gestures.,c:Distance yourself from the situation.
note: Physically and mentally remove yourself from aggressive drivers by slowing down, changing lanes, or pulling over safely; avoid eye contact and gestures.

question: True or False: A Merging lanes sign means you should be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to enter your lane.
options: a:False,b:True
note: A merging lanes sign indicates that two lanes will become one; drivers should be ready to either change lanes or allow others to merge safely.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the outside mirror on the side you plan to move to.,b:Turn your head to look over the shoulder toward the lane you will enter.,c:Flash your lights to warn other drivers.,d:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.
note: In addition to mirrors, physically turn your head to check blind spots before every lane change to ensure there are no vehicles you cannot see in mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Signal and keep your wheels straight.
note: Keep your wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn left so that if you are struck from behind you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: Should you avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid remaining alongside them and instead drop back or move ahead when safe.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:Alcohol will help the medicine work faster.,b:The medicine will reduce the effect of the alcohol.,c:The combination can multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medication.
note: Mixing alcohol with medications—prescription or OTC—can increase impairment and magnify side effects; a small amount of alcohol plus certain drugs can have effects similar to drinking many more alcoholic beverages.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (lose traction on water), what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to stop quickly.,b:Accelerate to regain traction.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.
note: If you hydroplane, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually; do not brake suddenly or make sharp steering inputs until traction returns.

question: If a person is convicted of leaving the scene of a crash, their driver license may be revoked for up to how long?
options: a:Six months,b:Three months,c:12 months
note: Conviction for leaving the scene of a motor vehicle crash can result in license revocation for up to one year.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, you should:
options: a:Pull to the left of the intersection and stop.,b:Remain where you are and wait,c:Continue through the intersection,d:Stop immediately inside the intersection.
note: If you're in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your high beam headlights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Do not use high beams in fog; use low beam headlights to improve visibility and avoid glare from reflected light.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Turn your lights on and off repeatedly.,c:Switch your lights to high beams.
note: If an oncoming vehicle's headlights are blinding you, glance toward the right edge of the road and follow the lane markings until the vehicle passes. Do not stare at the lights.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do regarding lights?
options: a:Use only your parking lights.,b:Turn off all lights to save the battery.,c:Leave your low-beam headlights on and turn on your emergency flashers.
note: If you stop on the roadside at night, get your vehicle out of traffic if possible, turn on your emergency flashers, and keep your low-beam headlights on so others can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which speed should you travel at?
options: a:At the speed of surrounding vehicles even if it exceeds the limit.,b:As fast as you feel comfortable.,c:Always at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,d:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions while obeying limits.
note: Choose a speed that matches road and weather conditions and legal limits; never exceed posted limits and slow down when conditions are poor."

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle passes.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or sirens, pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until it has passed.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:
options: a:Watch carefully for children walking near the road before proceeding.,b:Proceed as soon as the bus door closes.,c:Wait until children wave at you.,d:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, look for children walking and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What lighting should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in rainy conditions to improve your visibility without creating glare; high beams can reflect off rain and reduce visibility.

question: When it is very foggy, which lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.,c:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams will create glare and reduce visibility by reflecting light back at you.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed by a person?
options: a:Color of the drink.,b:Body weight and amount of food in the digestive tract.,c:Height only.,d:Intelligence only.
note: Absorption of alcohol depends on weight, biological sex, the amount of food in the stomach, and the number of drinks consumed; time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the road ahead is clear without checking.,b:Assuming the driver will hold steady speed if you signal.,c:Assuming the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield or make space for you; ensure there is room to complete the pass safely before you begin.

question: If poor weather makes it hard to see, you should do what regarding following distance?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead in poor visibility or slippery conditions to allow more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Keep a constant freeway speed as you travel down the ramp.,b:Slow down well before entering the ramp and stop on the shoulder.,c:Reduce your speed after you have moved onto the exit ramp.
note: Do not brake hard while still on the freeway; move onto the exit ramp and then slow to the posted ramp speed.

question: Do drivers have to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights if the bus is on a private road?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers are required to stop for a school bus using flashing red lights and stop arm whether the bus is on public or private roads.

question: If you are driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Passing it on a two-lane road.,c:Giving it extra space when merging.
note: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots along their sides. Avoid lingering beside them because the truck driver may not see you and may change lanes.

question: When in a line of traffic crossing a railroad with no signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Pass slower drivers while crossing the track.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way and proceed without checking.,c:Be sure there is room ahead so your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping.,d:Stop on the tracks to wait for the vehicle ahead.
note: Ensure there is sufficient space to completely clear the tracks before entering; never pass another vehicle near a railroad crossing."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see traffic without entering it.,b:Only if there is a pedestrian present.,c:You are not required to stop.,d:Anywhere within 20 feet of the intersection.
note: Stop at the nearest point before the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic; do not enter the intersection to gain a view."

question: When approaching a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Carefully drive around them on the sidewalk.,b:Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.,c:Honk your horn as you pass to alert them.
note: You must stop and remain stopped until a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is safely out of your path of travel; never honk or try to maneuver around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to nearby cross traffic that may cause a conflict.,b:Always stop even if no traffic is present.,c:Proceed without slowing if the road seems clear.
note: At a Yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard.

question: When entering a freeway from an on-ramp, the safest practice is to:
options: a:Use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and merge smoothly.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for a large gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the freeway so you can blend in safely; traffic already on the freeway has the right-of-way."

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Stop and exit your vehicle to watch.,c:Drive to the scene to offer help even if emergency services are present.,d:Speed past without slowing.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are directly involved or emergency help hasn't arrived; keep moving and remain alert for people or hazards."

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and you may change lanes or pass if safe.,d:It marks a bike lane only.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when safe."

question: Which influences the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The body weight of an individual,b:The amount of food in the stomach,c:How much time passes between drinks
note: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, the time between drinks, body weight, and food in the stomach; all these influence intoxication.

question: When faced with an aggressive driver, what is the best response?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Avoid eye contact,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: Remain calm, avoid escalating the situation, minimize contact, and put space between you and the aggressive driver whenever possible.

question: What should you do to stay alert when driving on a major highway?
options: a:Stay alert and keep your eyes moving.,b:Relax and stare at the center of the road.,c:Maintain a constant speed and stop scanning.
note: Keep your attention moving, scan ahead and to the sides, and be ready to react to hazards to avoid highway hypnosis and improve safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn before turning.,b:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.,c:Maintain your current speed and turn quickly.
note: Even on a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic that has the right-of-way before making a turn.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which should you avoid doing?
options: a:Keeping your seat belt fastened.,b:Pressing your head against the head restraint.,c:Bracing yourself and holding the steering wheel.,d:Releasing your seat belt.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace against the seatback and head restraint to reduce the risk of whiplash and injury."

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Leave the wheels unlocked.,b:Keep wheels facing straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,d:Turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road.
note: On uphill parking without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the road edge (to the right) so the vehicle will roll off the road rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: A red arrow on a traffic light means a driver must:
options: a:Slow and proceed with caution.,b:Only stop if pedestrians are present.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,d:Stop
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and stay stopped until the signal changes to a green light or arrow, unless posted signs indicate otherwise.

question: What is the most frequent cause of motorcycle accidents?
options: a:Inadequate road conditions.,b:Inattention by the motorcyclist.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle failing to yield the right-of-way and making a left turn in front of an oncoming motorcycle.
note: A large share of motorcycle crashes involve another vehicle turning left and failing to yield to an oncoming motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop line is present at an intersection, where must you stop?
options: a:In the crosswalk.,b:After the stop line.,c:At the stop line.,d:Ten feet before the stop line
note: Stop lines are painted across the roadway to show the point where you must stop when required by signs or signals."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before making a turn?
options: a:Use your signal.,b:Turn the wheel.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Signal at least three to four seconds before turning so other road users know your intentions.

question: Worn or bald tires affect vehicle control by:
options: a:Can make turning more difficult.,b:Are likely to hydroplane.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.
note: Tires with insufficient tread increase stopping distances, raise the risk of hydroplaning, and make steering less effective.

question: When driving on snow or ice, which action is recommended before descending a steep hill?
options: a:Follow another vehicle closely for guidance.,b:Pump the brakes continuously to keep them warm.,c:Shift to a low gear to maintain control.
note: Use a low gear going down steep, slippery hills to help control speed and avoid slipping; increase following distances and avoid sudden stops.

question: Under what condition may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:If your lane is next to a broken line that allows passing and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass where pavement markings and signs allow it, such as when the centerline is a broken line and it is safe to do so; never pass on curves, hills, or by driving on the shoulder.

question: Which practice helps prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Flash your lights continuously while braking.,b:Avoid sudden stops and slow gradually.,c:Maintain speed and stop abruptly when necessary.
note: Avoiding sudden stops, releasing the gas to slow before braking, and signaling deceleration all help drivers behind you react and reduce rear-end crash risk.

question: When following a large truck in bad weather, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,b:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Leave extra space when following large trucks because they require longer distances to stop and have larger blind spots.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane without stopping.,b:Stop in your lane and leave your lights off.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as possible.
note: If your vehicle breaks down, move it out of traffic if you can, activate your emergency flashers, and safely seek assistance. Make sure the vehicle is visible to other road users.

question: If you damage a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked car and the owner is not present, leave a note with your contact information securely attached to the vehicle and report the incident as required.

question: If a traffic signal shows a flashing yellow arrow in your lane, you may:
options: a:Proceed after coming to a complete stop.,b:Proceed without yielding because you have right-of-way.,c:Not turn until the light turns steady green.,d:Proceed in the arrow’s direction after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows you to turn in the indicated direction but only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians."

question: Highway signs that warn about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead; obey these signs to reduce the risk of accidents.

question: A major factor contributing to crashes that cause death or serious injury is:
options: a:Drivers transporting more than one child at a time.,b:Drivers driving while under the influence of alcohol or other drugs.,c:Drivers making frequent stops to rest on long trips.
note: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a leading factor in serious and fatal crashes.

question: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and you need to stop on snow or ice, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Release the brake and let the vehicle roll to a stop.,b:Pump the brakes to prevent them from locking.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly (do not pump).
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will automatically modulate braking to prevent wheel lock-up and help maintain steering control.

question: Sudden strong winds on highways:
options: a:Only affect large trucks and buses.,b:Only reduce visibility but not affect vehicle movement.,c:Can create problems for all vehicles and affect handling and visibility.,d:Have no effect on cars.
note: High winds can blow dust, reduce visibility, and physically move vehicles — affecting drivers of all vehicle types.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which circumstance?
options: a:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,b:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: When a vehicle's speed differs significantly from surrounding traffic, it increases the chance of conflicts and collisions.
